nodes.text: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT of 3PL Enablement Design Document – Version 1.0 __________ 22

This document is designed to outline the proposed 3PL enablement process for Supply Chain 
Architected for Logistics Execution (SCALE) at Travis Association for the Blind. The functional 
design outlined in this document is intended solely for use at the specified Travis Association for 
the Blind facility in Austin, TX. Future implementations at any other Travis Association for the 
Blind facilities will result in either change to this document or entirely new functional flows per 
facility. 
 
The objective of this document is to define the systemic and functional processes and scope 
from a Manhattan Associates’ (MA) SCALE perspective. This document serves as a reference 
throughout the 3PL enablement process for confirmation of approach and definition of tasks. It 
will also serve as a reference for Manhattan Associates’ customer support organization (CSO) 
after implementation, and potentially a reference point for any future Travis Association for the 
Blind implementations.

IMPORTANT NOTE 
 
Travis currently operates as a 3PL for a single customer (DLA). This customer has some 
contractual restrictions regarding physical access to their merchandizing. Based on the current 
contract, Travis would need to have a physical segregation (fence/wall) to keep DLA’s operation 
apart from any other operation at Travis’ warehouse. 
 
Travis is not envisioning to enable another 3PL operation in the near future, mainly because of 
the requirements of their current customer. 
 
This document will outline the requirements and recommendations to enable another 3PL.

STATISTICS 
Basic statistics of the Austin, TX Warehouse can be found below:

o ~480,000 sqft. 
o 1 shift (5am ~ 3:30pm / Mon~Fri) 
o Travis may have overtime or additional operation days if nedded

▪ 
The United States Marines and United States Air Force are the main 
customers for Travis 
• 
Inbound

o ~4,000 pallets per month 
 
WAREHOUSE LAYOUT

TECHNOLOGY 
Host: Rainbow Data Systems 
Middleware: Dell Boomi 
WM Platform: Windows 
Version: Active SCALE 
RF Vendor: Zebra 
MHE Vendor: Pack Size and EMIT Inc 
Label Printer: Zebra (203 dpi)  
Chrome Version: TBD

1. Travis will create a Company for each new 3PL customer added to their operation. 
2. The Item Master will have the Company. 
3. The SKU will be unique across companies. This is not a SCALE limitation, but having 
multiple companies with the same SKU may be a challenge for the users during work 
execution due to the use of VoCollect. 
4. The Storage Template will be defined depending on the item’s characteristics. 
5. The dimensions/weight will be maintained at the Unit of Measure level. 
6. The Treat as Loose flag will be maintained at the Unit of Measure level. 
7. Ideally Travis would need to configure new zones (locating, allocation and work) to keep 
the customers’ inventory apart from other customers. 
8. Travis may use permanent locations for items with high demand at picking locations. 
9. A new set of locating configuration (Locating rule assignment criteria, Locating rule 
assignment, Location selection and Locating rule) is required to be created per 
customer, based on the zones and companies. 
10. A new set of allocation configuration (Allocation rule assignment criteria, Allocation rule 
assignment, Allocation location selection and Allocation rule) is required to be created 
per customer, based on the zones and companies. 
11. Travis may create a new Wave flow and Wave master with specific requirements for the 
customer. Travis can also opt to use a standard Wave flow/master for all customers, as 
long as the wave flow steps are not company specific. 
12. The Item Master, Receipt Download and Shipment Download should be downloaded 
into SCALE by Travis’ middleware provider. This is a Manhattan Associates 
recommendation to keep the logic to convert the data provided by the customer into a 
format that SCALE recognizes (XML). 
13. The Item Balance Upload, Inventory Transactions Upload, Receiving Upload and 
Shipping Upload should be generated as XML files by SCALE into separate folders, one 
per customer, at the Azure Storage. From there, Travis’ middleware should pick the files 
and convert the information into the format that Travis’ customer requires. 
14. In case the customer requires the use of Lot, Travis will be able to active lot tracking at 
the Item Master.
a. Travis understands that the use of lot tracked items represents a change to their

current operation that could affect Receiving, Picking, Replenishment, Cycle 
Count, Inventory Management, Packing, Outbound QC, etc. 
b. SCALE is fully prepared to work with lot tracked items, but the operational

changes need to be evaluated by Travis to define new SOPs. 
15. Travis will test the Blind Receiving available in Warehouse Mobile on the current 
SCALE’s version (24.7.2575). When the original design was made this feature was not 
yet available. 
16. Travis will test the Shipping Container QC available in Warehouse Mobile on the current 
SCALE’s version (24.7.2575). When the original design was made this feature was not 
yet available. 
17. Travis will test the Status Change available in Warehouse Mobile on the current 
SCALE’s version (24.7.2575). When the original design was made this feature was not 
yet available. 
18. Other configurations and processes not mentioned in this document should be kept as 
originally designed in the Solution Design Document.

Travis downloads & uploads information into SCALE using XML file-based methods of 
interfacing. 
 
This allows Travis to create records with key information for downloads, and SCALE 
reads this key information to process the download into the SCALE production tables. 
This method also allows Travis to read key information from SCALE’s upload interface 
records.  
 
Each interface touch point below can be run manually as well as through scheduled jobs 
as defined by Travis Association for the Blind. The specific schedule can depend on the 
Host System, warehouse processing times, and SCALE interface execution times. 
 
Warehouse alerts can be configured to notify Travis when a download or upload 
interface transaction has failed for any reason. 
 
1.0 
DOWNLOAD FROM HOST TO SCALE

1.1 
Download data 
 
Travis will download the following data into SCALE: 
o Item Master 
o Receipt Download 
o Shipment Download 
 
1.2 
Download architecture 
 
Travis will use their middleware (Boomi) to download information to SCALE. Boomi must 
receive/pull the necessary information from Travis’ customers, translate that information 
into SCALE’s format and then generate the expected XML file. 
 
The downloaded files will be stored in a single Azure Storage folder (/ils/Interface/Input).

1.3 
Item Master 
 
The item master file is maintained within the Host. Conversion quantities, weights, and 
dimensions are also maintained through this Item Master Download as those pieces of 
information are available in the host. The middleware receives information from the host 
system and downloads a record into the SCALE Item Master when an item is modified or 
created. If an item already exists in the Item Master, then the record is flagged as a 
change, and SCALE updates the existing item with the latest information bridged from 
the host. Key pieces of information include (but are not limited to) the following: 
 
o Item Master Level:

▪ 
Item (SKU/NSN) 
▪ 
Description 
▪ 
Company 
▪ 
Cross Reference 
▪ 
Packing Class 
▪ 
Item Class 
▪ 
Storage Template 
▪ 
Item Unit of Measure Level:

• 
Item Dimensions 
• 
Item Weight 
• 
Movement Class (A, B, C) 
▪ 
Item Categories 
 
Note: SKUs at Travis are referred to internally as NSNs and this terminology may be 
used throughout the remainder of this document. 
 
Config Note: To be able to use the XML download interface option, the ‘Item XML 
Download’ must be enabled under the ‘Interface Process’ configuration. 
 
1.4 
Receipts 
 
Receipts should be downloaded into SCALE in advance, so the users can receive 
against an existing receipt. Travis may also use Blind receiving for unexpected returns, 
although this process requires previous agreements with Travis’ customers. 
 
Note: The receipts must have the Company field interfaced at the header level.

The information downloaded to SCALE from Travis will always contain both header and 
detail level information. Container Level Receipt data, if available from customer, could 
also be interfaced in advance to speed up the check-in process.

available from customer)

1.5 
Shipments 
 
The shipments information will flow through Boomi which will be responsible for any 
conversion/formatting required. Once formatted, the Shipments will be passed onto 
SCALE via XML file-based interfaces. Shipment data is sent with a warehouse-specific 
shipment header, one or more shipment details, and optional shipment comments. The 
shipment header contains information such as customer, customer address, ship to 
address, carrier, and scheduled ship date information. The shipment detail is the item 
level detail for the shipment containing information such as item and ordered quantity. 
Comments can be linked to the shipment header or details to validate additional 
processing requirements within the warehouse. Until the shipment has been waved, 
SCALE can process updates and deletions from the host against the shipment. 
 
Note: The shipments must have the Company field interfaced at the header level.

2.1 
Upload data 
 
SCALE will upload the following data: 
o Receipt Confirmation 
o Shipment Confirmation 
o Inventory Transactions 
o Item Balance 
 
2.2 
Upload architecture 
 
SCALE will generate the upload data into different Azure Storage folders, based on the 
Interface Process configuration. These configurations should leverage base SCALE 
criterias to generate the files into the corresponding customer’s folder. 
 
From the Azure Storage, middleware (Boomi) should read the information per folder and 
convert the information back to customer’s host systems. 
 
2.3 Receipt Confirmation 
 
The Interface Data option creates the receipt upload files from SCALE for all receipts 
that have reached the trailing status ‘In Putaway’ or have been closed manually. The 
receipt upload files are the output of the receiving processes within SCALE. The upload 
includes receipt header, receipt detail, and receipt container level information. As each 
receipt container reaches ‘In Putaway’ status (Container Level Upload), the interface 
sends information to the host system to allow that receipt’s inventory to be 
acknowledged as present in the facility.  
 
For Travis Association for the Blind, the upload will be performed at Container level 
when the status of the receipt reaches ‘In Putaway’. 
 
Config Notes:

A new Receiving interface upload criteria should be created and configured for 
each customer, using the Company as the filter attribute.

A new Interface Process Detail should be created and configured for each 
customer, using the criteria created in the previous step. It should also indicate 
an exclusive folder per customer.

2.4 Shipment Confirmation 
 
The Interface Data option creates the shipment upload files from SCALE for all 
shipments that have reached status ‘Closed’ (shipment has been loaded to the truck and 
truck has left the warehouse). The shipment upload files are the output of the outbound 
process within SCALE. These files are generated after the execution of the Shipping 
Load confirmation. The upload includes shipment header, shipment detail, shipment 
comment, and shipping container information. 
 
For Travis Association for the Blind, Shipment uploads are created only at Closed (900) 
status.

A new Shipping interface upload criteria should be created and configured for 
each customer, using the Company as the filter attribute.

A new Interface Process Detail should be created and configured for each 
customer, using the criteria created in the previous step. It should also indicate 
an exclusive folder per customer.

2.5 Inventory Transactions 
 
SCALE maintains 4-wall inventory at a detailed level and communicates any changes in 
inventory levels to Travis through the Inventory Transactions Interface. All movements 
and changes in inventory are eligible to be uploaded (Adhoc adjustments, cycle count 
adjustments, status changes, etc). 
 
Travis can use the base configuration in SCALE to not interface specific transactions, 
based on their business requirements. To achieve that, the Adjustment Type used to 
generate the inventory transaction should have the field Include in interface uploads 
unchecked.

A new Inventory transaction interface upload criteria should be created and 
configured for each customer, using the Company as the filter attribute.

A new Interface Process Detail should be created and configured for each 
customer, using the criteria created in the previous step. It should also indicate 
an exclusive folder per customer.

2.6 Item Balance 
 
The total on-hand inventory for a given item and inventory status can be uploaded to the 
host system on-demand through the Interface Data option in SCALE, or on a scheduled 
basis as configured in the Scheduled Job option. Any time the total on hand quantities 
are needed to compare against the host system, this option can be run and sent to the 
host for reporting & comparison purposes. 
 
Config Notes:

A new Item balance interface upload criteria should be created and configured 
for each customer, using the Company as the filter attribute.

A new Interface Process Detail should be created and configured for each 
customer, using the criteria created in the previous step. It should also indicate 
an exclusive folder per customer.

In order to select the putaway locations based on the Company, a new set of 
configurations must be created in SCALE. These configurations will assign a locating 
rule based on a criteria. Multiple configurations may need to be created for each 
customer to accommodate the requirements of storage of products and the unit of 
measure being received.

3.1 
Location selection 
 
One or more Location selection configuration must be created. The location selection will 
indicate which locations should be evaluated during the locating process. Usually there 
are a few location selections based on the zones and the unit of measure that should be 
stored in that zone (EA, CS, PL).

The locating rules must be created according to the requirements to store the items 
received. A locating rule may have several detail records with different location 
selections and strategies.

3.3 
Locating rule assignment criteria 
 
The criteria must use the company at the receipt detail as a filter.

3.4 
Locating rule assignment 
 
This is the configuration that will tighten together the locating rule and the criteria, to 
indicate to SCALE which locating rule should be used during the check-in.

Replenishment uses allocation rules to identify the inventory that should be allocated. 
These rules should use the zones defined for each customer. 
 
5.0 
CYCLE COUNT

Both the Cycle Count Master and Cycle Count Quick Plan can leverage the use of the 
zones and/or company to filter the inventory that should be counted. 
 
The frequency of the cycle count depends on the contract with the 3PL customer, so its 
recommended to create the configurations for each customer to better accommodate 
any requirements changes.

In order to select the inventory that is going to be shipped based on the Company, a new 
set of configurations must be created in SCALE. These configurations will assign an 
allocation rule based on a criteria. Multiple configurations may be created to 
accommodate the business requirements during the outbound process.

6.1 
Allocation location selection 
 
One or more Allocation location selection configuration may be created. The allocation 
location selection will indicate which locations should be evaluated during the allocation 
process. Usually there are a few allocation location selections based on the zones and 
the unit of measure that should be stored in that zone (EA, CS, PL).

The allocation rules must be created according to the requirements to assign the 
inventory to the orders. An allocation rule may have several detail records with different 
allocation location selections and strategies.

6.3 
Allocation rule assignment criteria 
 
The criteria must use the company at the shipment detail as a filter.

6.4 
Allocation rule assignment 
 
This is the configuration that will tighten together the allocation rule and the criteria, to 
indicate to SCALE which allocation rule should be used during the waving process.

6.5 
Rule Assignment 
 
To make the above configuration work, it is important to add the wave step Rule 
Assignment to the wave flows. This wave step will evaluate the configurations defined 
above and will assign the corresponding Allocation Rule to the shipment lines.
This wave step needs to be placed before the Allocation wave step.

Travis can keep using the same Wave Flows and Wave Masters as they use today. In 
case special requirements from a new 3PL customer is needed, Travis can request to 
make changes to existing Override Data Wave Step or to create new ones to 
accommodate the business requirements. 
 
8.0 
WORK MANAGEMENT

Travis may need to define different priorities based on customers’ requests. Travis 
already deals with orders/work that requires an elevation on the priority. 
 
Travis will need to develop a SOP for this process. 
 
9.0 
PICKING

Travis may continue using the current Work Types for most of their picking processes. In 
case they need to have specific people working on different zones, this can be achieved 
by using the Work Profile’s Work Zone configuration. 
 
 
10.0 PACKING 
 
10.1 
VAS (Value Added Services) 
 
The criteria used to assign VAS to the containers may also leverage the Company as a 
filter. In case Travis needs to add VAS to specific customers only, a new VAS Activity 
Criteria needs to be created and used on the VAS Activity screen.

The VAS Assignment wave step needs to be added after the Container Creation wave 
step, so SCALE can evaluate the containers based on the VAS Activity Criteria. Multiple 
criterias can be created. SCALE will evaluate all the active criterias during the VAS 
Assignment wave step.

Note: VAS can be assigned only when containers are created in Wave. 
 
10.2 
QC Process (Order Verification/OV) 
 
Similar to VAS, the QC Assignment Criteria and the QC Assignment can be created to 
accommodate requests from 3PL customers related to the Outbound QC verification. 
 
Note: QC can be assigned automatically only when containers are created in Wave.
